Kernel side validation, error codes, permission checks and fault handling internals.

findings.text: User tracing ABI fixes three names: base system user_events, multi system user_events_multi, and dynamic prefix letter u plus colon. Consumers match system strings against these spellings.
Dynamic field location packs offset and size into one 32 bit word with size in the upper half and offset in the lower half, using a 16 bit shift of size combined with offset.

Registration flags use bit zero for persistence across last close and bit one for allowing multiple formats per event. Bit two is a sentinel marking the start of non ABI values, so only lower bits are stable.

Registration descriptor is byte packed and versioned by its leading size. It carries enable bit index, enable byte width, flag half word, 64 bit enable address, 64 bit name and argument string pointer, and returns a 32 bit write index for later data writes. All but the trailing index are inputs.

Unregistration descriptor is byte packed and versioned by leading size. It carries disable bit index, two reserved fields that callers set to zero with 8 bit then 16 bit width, and a 64 bit disable address. No output field is defined.

Diag control uses magic asterisk with three numbers: zero registers with bidirectional transfer of a registration descriptor pointer, one deletes with write transfer of a name string pointer, two unregisters with write transfer of an unregistration descriptor pointer.
Userfaultfd uses hex AA both as ioctl magic and as requested API number, with a distinct new device construction code at subcode zero and a user mode only creation flag value one.

Sub operation numbers run zero through ten for register, unregister, wake, copy, zero page, move, write protect, continue, poison, read write protect and set mode, with hex 3F reserved for the API handshake.

Each sub operation has an ioctl wrapper bound to its descriptor: handshake uses API structure, register uses register structure, unregister and wake use range structure, copy, zero page, move, write protect, continue, poison, read write protect and set mode each use the structure sharing their name. Handshake plus all but unregister, wake and set mode exchange both ways, unregister and wake read back, set mode writes in.

Fault and event message is packed, starting with an event byte plus reserved bytes and word and long, followed by a variant payload. Page fault carries flags, faulting address and thread id when enabled. Fork carries new descriptor. Remap carries source, destination and length. Remove carries start and end. A reserved variant holds three 64 bit spares.
Event codes are hex 12 for page fault, hex 13 for fork, hex 14 for remap, hex 15 for remove and hex 16 for unmap.
Page fault reason flags occupy low bits: bit zero marks write access, bit one marks write protect cause, bit two marks minor fault cause, bit three marks read write protect cause.

API handshake structure carries a requested API number, a feature word used both to request and to report support, and an ioctl capability mask reported by the kernel. Page fault delivery and write access indication are always active once the API number matches, without needing feature bits.

Feature bits span zero to eighteen: write protect fault reporting, fork event, remap event, remove event, missing support on hugetlbfs, missing support on shmem, unmap event, signal bus instead of event, thread id reporting, minor support on hugetlbfs, minor support on shmem, exact fault address without page masking, write protection on hugetlbfs and shmem, write protection applied to unpopulated entries, poison support, async write protect auto resolve, move support, read write protect tracking, and async read write protect auto resolve.

Range descriptor holds start and length as 64 bit values. Register descriptor embeds a range, a mode word and a kernel reported ioctl mask kept last because its tail is not read from user. Modes use bit zero for missing, bit one for write protect, bit two for minor and bit three for read write protect. Aggregate masks define the full mode set, the full feature set, the always available ioctl set, the full per range ioctl set and a basic per range subset omitting move and zero page.

Copy descriptor holds destination, source and length with a mode word and a trailing bytes copied result that the kernel writes and does not read in. Zero page descriptor holds a range with mode and trailing pages filled result with the same write only tail rule. Copy modes offer no wake and write protect on copy when that protection is advertised for the range. Zero page mode offers no wake.

Move descriptor holds destination, source and length with mode and trailing bytes moved result that is write only. Continue and poison descriptors each hold a range with mode and trailing written result that is write only past the mode. Move modes offer no wake and permission to allow holes at source. Continue modes offer no wake and write protect on map when advertised. Poison mode offers no wake.

Write protect and read write protect descriptors each hold a range plus mode with no trailing result. Setting the protect bit applies protection while clearing it removes previously applied protection. Both offer a no wake option, with waking only mattering when removing protection in reply to a fault. A separate toggle structure carries enable and disable masks for runtime async switching, currently supporting async read write protect, and forbids setting the same bit in both masks.
Legacy time setting structure holds access and modification times as old kernel time values in that order.

Host identity layouts grow across generations: old length constant eight backs five nine byte names, new length constant sixty four backs five sixty five byte names in the middle form and six new length plus one names adding domain in the newest form.

Blanking states are zero for no blanking, one for vertical suspend, two for horizontal suspend, three as the combination of both meaning power down, with the combined value also serving as the maximum.

VFIO reports API version zero, uses semicolon as ioctl type and one hundred as ioctl base. IOMMU and extension numbers covered here run one through ten: type one, SPAPR TCE, type one v2, DMA with confidential computing, EEH, reserved nesting implying v2, SPAPR TCE v2, no IOMMU, unmap all and update address.

Capability header carries 16 bit identifier, 16 bit version and 32 bit byte offset to next capability. Group status carries total size and flags with bit zero meaning viable and bit one meaning container already set.

Device info carries total size, flags, region count as max index plus one, interrupt count as max index plus one, offset to first capability and padding. Defined flag bits mark reset support, PCI, platform, AMBA, CCW, AP, FSL MC, capability presence and CDX in order from bit zero to eight. Atomic compare capability appends a header, flag word and reserved word with bits for 32, 64 and 128 bit compare widths.

VFIO ioctls add offsets zero through seven to the base: get API version, check extension, set IOMMU model, get group status, set container, unset container, get device file descriptor and get device info.

Device API names fix five spellings for PCI, platform, AMBA, CCW and AP transports. Device information capability identifiers use one through five for ZPCI base, group, utility, PFIP and PCI atomic compare.

Handshake provides feature and ioctl capability data that determines which later events and per range operations are available. Registering a range selects missing, write protect, minor or read write protect tracking, faults are then resolved with copy, zero page, move, continue or protection updates, while fork, remap, remove and unmap messages only appear when their features were negotiated.
Registration yields a write index tied to an enable address and bit, data writes use that index while enabled, then unregistration by address and bit or deletion by name releases the event.

Group moves between unbound and container bound as reported by its status flag, with set and unset operations changing the binding after viability and extension checks, while per device descriptors and capability queries are used once the group is bound.

Packed layout keeps user and kernel views identical for registration, unregistration and fault messages. Leading size and argsz fields version each structure, capability chains use byte offsets with zero terminating, and trailing result words are kernel written only and must sit last.

No wake only affects whether faulting waiters are awakened after a successful operation and is meaningless when applying protection rather than releasing it. Removing protection normally wakes the faulting task. The register ioctl mask gates which per range operations and on the fly protect modes are legal.

Callers must zero reserved fields, must not rely on masked page offset unless exact address was negotiated, must expect signal bus delivery instead of messages when that feature is on, must not set the same toggle bit in both enable and disable, and must handle that async modes auto resolve faults without delivering messages.
